newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian call steady, gilts market awaits bond issue.
newsitem.headline: Indian call steady, gilts market awaits bond issue.

text.p: Indian call money was quoted in the 2.75-3.25 percent range in early Wednesday trade, unchanged from Tuesday's close and dealers said they expected rates to remain at the same level during the day.
They said funds supply was good and rates will harden only if liquidity is drained by a government bond issue.
"The large amount of excess liquidity warrants an auction announcement by the Reserve Bank of India," ICICI Securities and Finance Company said in a debt market commentary.
Dealers said good deposit growth and poor demand for credit from corporates had saddled banks with excess liquidity.
Government securities were quoted higher in early trade but no deals were struck, said a dealer at a state-run bank.

"Some traders have become cautious as they feel prices have already risen too much," he said. "There is also a feeling that a new bond issue is around the corner. This is checking trade... but prices should remain firm, at current levels."
